overview.roadmapBody: Phase 1 delivers identity, workspaces, roles, clients and projects with server-side authorization and audit logging.

clients.subtitle: Every client in this workspace.

clients.noMatchesHint: Try a different search term or clear the status filters.

projects.assignedOnly: Showing the projects you are assigned to.
projects.forbidden: Your role does not include access to projects.
projects.emptyHint: Create a project to start planning work for a client.
projects.noneAssigned: You are not assigned to any project yet
projects.noneAssignedHint: A project manager assigns people to projects. Ask to be added to the work you are on.
projects.noMatchesHint: Try a different search term or clear the status filters.

projects.spendPaused: Campaigns under this project may not spend.

fields.clientLocked: A project cannot be moved to another client.
fields.name: Project name
fields.endsBeforeStart: The end date cannot be before the start date.

form.description: A new project starts in planning. Campaigns can only spend once it is active.

administration.subtitle: People, roles and the record of what happened.
administration.forbidden: Your role does not include workspace administration.
administration.auditForbidden: Your role does not include access to the audit log.
administration.noAuditHint: Sign-ins and changes to clients, projects and people appear here as they happen.

integrations.subtitle: Ad platforms this workspace can read from, and which projects may read what.
integrations.forbidden: Your role does not include access to integrations.
integrations.awaitingAccessBody_one: {{count}} platform cannot be connected yet. These need credentials or programme approval from the provider — an account-owner action, not a setting here. digitalSmart will not show figures it cannot actually retrieve.
integrations.awaitingAccessBody_other: {{count}} platforms cannot be connected yet. These need credentials or programme approval from the providers — account-owner actions, not settings here. digitalSmart will not show figures it cannot actually retrieve.
integrations.noCapabilities: No published API yet, so there is nothing we can honestly offer for this platform.
integrations.blockedBody: Needs: {{keys}}. These are issued by the provider.
integrations.credentialsDescription: The platform's own API credentials, issued to Smart Code.
integrations.neverClientPassword: Never enter a client's platform password. digitalSmart does not store them, and does not need them: access comes from OAuth, Business Manager sharing or partner access.
integrations.sandboxHint: To exercise the workflow before a provider grants access, enter “sandbox” in every field. You will get clearly labelled SANDBOX accounts and no invented figures.
integrations.bindingsDescription: A project reads an ad account only if it is granted here. Discovering an account does not expose it to anyone.
integrations.selectProjectHint: Pick a project to see which ad accounts it may read, and to grant or revoke access.
integrations.noAccountsHint: Connect a platform and find its accounts first. Until then there is nothing to grant.

analytics.subtitle: Performance across every platform a project is bound to.
analytics.forbidden: Your role does not include access to performance analytics.
analytics.loadFailed: Performance data could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.

trend.title: {{metric}} over time
trend.hint: Select a figure above to plot it
trend.aria: {{metric}} by day from {{start}} to {{end}}. Days with no delivery are left blank rather than shown as zero.

efficiency.title: Efficiency against scale
efficiency.question: Which campaigns deserve more budget, and which are expensive at size?
efficiency.aria: Each point is a campaign, positioned by spend against cost per acquisition. Lower and further right is better.

empty.title: No performance data for this period
empty.description: Either nothing was delivered in this range, or no ad account is bound to a project you can see. Connect a platform and bind an account to a project to start syncing.
empty.breakdown: Nothing to break down for this period.

live.label: Live
live.help: Read from the platform within the freshness window.

synced.label: Synced
synced.help: Synced from the platform, though the freshness window has moved on.

stale.label: Stale
stale.help: Older than the freshness threshold. Shown, but a sync has not succeeded recently.
stale.notice: these figures are older than the freshness threshold. A sync has not completed recently, so treat them as indicative until it does.

partial.label: Partial
partial.help: The sync covered only part of the range, so totals understate reality.
partial.notice: the last sync covered only part of this range, so these totals are lower than the real ones. They will rise when the sync completes.

sandbox.label: Sandbox
sandbox.help: From sandbox fixtures. Not real performance, and never to be shared with a client.
sandbox.notice: these are sandbox figures from test fixtures, not real performance. They exist so the product can be used before a platform grants API access. Do not share them with a client or act on them.

manual.label: Manual
manual.help: Entered by a person — an offline conversion or a spend adjustment.
manual.notice: part of this includes figures entered by hand rather than synced from a platform.

estimated.label: Estimated
estimated.help: A projection, not a measurement. Never totalled with actuals.
estimated.notice: this is a projection based on past performance, not a measurement, and it is not a guarantee of results.

campaigns.drillHint: Select a row to open its {{level}}s

dashboards.title: Dashboards
dashboards.subtitle: Build a canvas of the figures a client actually asks about.
dashboards.saveFailed: The dashboard could not be saved.
dashboards.loadFailed: Dashboards could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
dashboards.editHint: Reorder and resize with the controls on each widget. Nothing is saved until you choose Save.

editor.needsTwoMetrics: This chart plots one metric against another, so it needs two.
editor.title: Title
editor.titleHint: Optional. Leave blank to use the chart type.

widget.noMetric: This widget has no metric to show.

aria.scatter: {{metric}} plotted against each other, one point per {{dimension}}.

emptyCanvas.title: This dashboard has no widgets yet
emptyCanvas.description: Open it for editing and add the first one.

none.title: No dashboards yet
none.description: A dashboard is a canvas of the figures you look at most. Build one and share it with the workspace or keep it to yourself.

forbidden.title: No access to budgets
forbidden.description: Your role does not include budgets. Budgets carry what a client agreed to spend, so access is granted deliberately.

errors.save: The budget could not be saved.
errors.allocations: The allocations could not be saved.
errors.approve: The budget could not be approved.
errors.archive: The budget could not be archived.
errors.delete: The budget could not be deleted.

allocations.title: Allocation
allocations.none: Nothing is allocated yet. Split the budget by platform to compare it with spend.
allocations.label: Label

pacing.risksOverspend: On course to go over the budget
pacing.risksUnderDelivery: On course to land short of the budget
pacing.allocationsCaption: Each allocation against the spend that landed inside it.

chart.description: Cumulative spend against an even pace. Approved {{budget}}, spent {{spent}}.

mediaPlanner.title: Media planner
mediaPlanner.subtitle: What a client agreed to, how it is split across platforms, and how it is running.

empty.title: No budgets yet
empty.description: A budget records what a client agreed to spend, and is what pacing is measured against.

detail.amountFixed: Approved, so the amount and period are fixed. To change them, archive this budget and approve a new one — both stay on the record.

form.name: Name
form.clientHint: A budget belongs to a client. Leave the project unset for a budget the whole client spends.
form.notesHint: Never shown to a client, and deliberately left out of the change log.
form.notApprovedYet: Saved as a draft. {{amount}} is not committed until somebody approves it.

budgetCalculator.title: Budget calculator
budgetCalculator.subtitle: What a budget might buy, or what a target might cost — from this workspace's own delivery.
budgetCalculator.ownDataOnly: Rates come from this workspace's own past delivery. No industry averages are used.
budgetCalculator.error: The estimate could not be worked out.
budgetCalculator.noProjection: Nothing can be estimated for this platform yet.

fields.windowHint: A longer window is steadier; a shorter one reflects how the account runs now.

empty.title: Nothing to estimate from
empty.description: No platform in this workspace has enough observed delivery yet. Connect a platform and sync it, and the rates will follow.

tracking.title: Tracking Center
tracking.subtitle: What is measuring each client's work, what counts as success there, and whether any of it is actually working.
tracking.loadFailed: Could not load the tracking picture. Try again in a moment.

issues.title: What needs attention
issues.noneBody: Every connected source is reporting, and every conversion has been seen. This list is empty when tracking is working — that is what it is for.

sources.title: What is measuring
sources.name: Source
sources.emptyTitle: Nothing is measuring this work yet
sources.emptyBody: Connect an analytics property, a store or an ad account, then bind it to this client.

conversions.title: What counts as success
conversions.emptyBody: Until one is, no report can say what success means for this client.

register.title: Add an analytics property
register.subtitle: Every property this workspace's Google connection can read, including the ones for clients you no longer work with. Check the site before you pick.
register.none: The connected account can read no properties.
register.unavailable: Google Analytics is not connected yet, or its authorisation is not complete. Fix that on the integrations page.
register.failed: Could not register that property. It may already be registered for this client.

sync.skipped: {{name}} has nothing to read — it is a source somebody fills in by hand.

editor.name: Name
editor.meaningHint: Chosen by you. Nothing here is inferred from the event name.
editor.mappingsHint: A raw name counts towards this conversion only because it is listed here. One property's “contact” is a form; another's is a phone tap.
editor.suggestionsHint: Events the property's owner marked as key. Adding one fills in the name; the meaning is still yours to choose.
editor.oncePerSessionNote: Some of these are counted once per session, so two in one visit count as one. Worth knowing before reconciling against orders.
editor.intentWarning: This is a signal of intent, not a completed action. Count it if you mean to, but do not report it as a lead or a sale.
editor.saveFailed: Could not save. The server gave no reason — check the connection and try again.

observed.title: What has actually been seen
observed.subtitle: Against what each client said success is, over the last {{days}} days
observed.caveat: Intent signals are in this chart because somebody defined them, and they are a different colour because they are a different thing: a tap is not a conversation and a form begun is not a form submitted. Nothing here is totalled. "Never seen" means the event was looked for and has not happened — usually the most actionable row on the page.
observed.emptyBody: Define what counts as success for a client and this chart will show whether any of it is happening.
observed.aria: Observed counts for each defined event over the last {{days}} days, with conversions and intent signals shown separately and never totalled.

commerce.title: Store revenue
commerce.subtitle: What a client's stores sold, according to one named authority. These figures are never mixed across sources — they measure different things and they will disagree.
commerce.loadFailed: Could not load the revenue picture. Try again in a moment.
commerce.trendTooShort: A single day is not a trend. Widen the period to see one.

source.label: Revenue according to
source.hint: There is no combined figure. A store counts invoices; analytics counts what a browser reported; an ad platform reports what it believes it caused.

claim.invoiced: {{source}} invoiced this money. It is the closest thing to what the client actually earned.
claim.reported: {{source}} reported this. It is a measurement of sales, not a record of them, and it will not match the store's own total.
claim.modelled: This is modelled, not recorded. {{source}} revenue is a model's output and must not be presented to a client as actual.

metrics.noOrders: No paid order in this period, so there is no average to show.

attribution.title: Where the revenue came from
attribution.hint: Only what the orders themselves carried. An order with no campaign parameters is unattributed, not assigned to whatever was running — and the confidence on each row is the weakest link inside it.

breakdown.empty: Nothing to show for this period.

chart.label: Net revenue by day from {{from}} to {{until}}, totalling {{total}}.

empty.title: No {{source}} revenue in this period
empty.body: Either nothing sold, or no store is connected for this authority yet. The integrations page is where a store is connected.

commerce.pending_one: {{count}} order is placed and not yet paid for, worth {{amount}}. Not counted above — cash on delivery becomes revenue when it is collected, and some of it comes back instead.
commerce.pending_other: {{count}} orders are placed and not yet paid for, worth {{amount}} together. Not counted above — cash on delivery becomes revenue when it is collected, and some of it comes back instead.
commerce.trendSubtitle: Refunds are drawn beside net revenue rather than netted away: a flat month because returns rose is a different problem from a month nobody bought in.

empty.title: Nothing to plot yet
empty.body: No figures have been recorded for this period. That is not the same as zero — a chart would show a flat line, which would be wrong.

unavailable.title: Not available
unavailable.body: This platform does not report the figures this chart needs.

leads.title: Lead Center
leads.subtitle: Every enquiry a client received, how far it got, and — beside it rather than inside it — how many taps and part-filled forms were counted over the same days.
leads.loadFailed: Could not load the Lead Center. Try again in a moment.
leads.mixedCurrency: These leads carried {{count}} different currencies, so their totals are not shown: a sum of two currencies is not a larger number, it is not a number. Filter to one client to see a total.

source.label: Recorded by people, not measured by a platform

denied.title: The Lead Center is not part of your access
denied.body: It carries prospects' names and contact details, so it is limited to the roles that work the pipeline. Ask a workspace owner if you need it.

metric.noClosed: Nothing has closed yet, so there is nothing to divide by. This is not a win rate of zero.
metric.noLeads: No leads arrived in this period.
metric.noWonValue: No won lead carried a value.
metric.mixedCurrency: The won leads were in more than one currency, so there is no total to average.

pipeline.title: How far leads got
pipeline.subtitle: Of the leads that arrived in the last {{days}} days
pipeline.whyNoQualified: Qualified is not a step here. The figure available is how many leads sit at that stage now, and a lead that has since been won passed through it without being counted — so putting it between "got through" and "won" would show the funnel narrowing and then widening.
pipeline.emptyBody: Nothing arrived in the last {{days}} days. That is not a funnel of zeroes — there is nothing to draw.
pipeline.aria: How far the leads of the last {{days}} days got, as four stages from arrived to won.

signals.title: Taps and forms begun
signals.subtitle: Counted over the same {{days}} days
signals.comparison: {{signals}} counted, {{leads}} leads. The gap is expected and no percentage is offered: the same person taps several times, or taps and then phones instead.
signals.emptyBody: No tap or form-start events have been observed for this scope. That may mean tracking is not installed — the Tracking Center says which.
signals.aria: Counted taps and form starts over the last {{days}} days, by event name.

bySource.title: By route
bySource.subtitle: Which way the enquiry arrived
bySource.caveat: A route marked "not measured" was entered or imported by hand. Those are real leads and must not be reported as campaign results.

byCampaign.title: By campaign
byCampaign.subtitle: What the lead itself carried
byCampaign.caveat: A campaign here is what the lead arrived tagged with — not a model's opinion of which campaign deserves the credit. Leads that carried nothing are shown as their own row rather than left out.

breakdown.folded: The smallest {{count}} rows are summed into "other": that row has no win rate and no value, because averaging rates with different denominators produces a figure that is none of theirs.
breakdown.emptyBody: No leads arrived in the last {{days}} days.
breakdown.aria: {{title}}, as leads per row over the last {{days}} days.

list.title: The pipeline
list.subtitle: Newest first. Choose a lead to see everything recorded for that person.
list.caption: Leads, with their route, stage, and how long somebody took to respond.
list.emptyBody: Nothing has been recorded for this scope.
list.moveFailed: Could not move the lead. Try again in a moment.

journey.title: Everything recorded
journey.pickBody: Everything recorded for that person — their enquiries and their orders — appears here.
journey.singleTouch: One record, nothing else recorded. This is not a journey yet.
journey.earliest: The earliest record carrying an attribution was a {{record}}, tagged {{campaign}}. That is a fact about that record, not a decision about which touch earned the credit.
journey.noAttribution: Carried no campaign of its own.
journey.emptyBody: No contact details on this lead could be matched to anything else, which is common and honest.

attribution.title: Attribution
attribution.subtitle: Which campaign earned the money — under a model you choose, from an authority you choose, with the share of the period it accounts for stated before the campaigns are.
attribution.loadFailed: Could not load the attribution. Try again in a moment.

denied.title: Attribution is not part of your access
denied.body: It is a view of a client's revenue against their spend, so it is limited to the roles that read analytics. Ask a workspace owner if you need it.

model.label: Model
model.hint: Each one answers a different question, so there is no default. One of these is a record; the rest are claims.

source.label: Revenue from
source.hint: The authority that counts the money. A figure from one cannot be mixed with another.

lookback.label: Look back
lookback.hint: How far back to search for an earlier conversion by the same person. A different window credits different campaigns.

coverage.title: How much of the period this accounts for
coverage.explain: {{named}} of the attributed orders name a campaign rather than only a channel. The rest are counted but not placed on a campaign row.
coverage.warning: These campaigns account for a minority of the period's revenue. The rest arrived with no marketing information and is not divided among them — it is unknown, which is different from zero. Treat the rows below as a sample, not as the month.

campaigns.title: Attributed revenue by campaign
campaigns.subtitle: Under {{model}}. A grey bar is revenue that cannot be put beside spend; the table says why.
campaigns.unmatchedSpend: {{amount}} of ad spend was on campaigns no order mentioned. That is a tagging problem with a size, not a gap in the report.
campaigns.noSpend: No ad spend was found for this period, so no row can carry a return on it.
campaigns.emptyBody: No order in this period carried marketing information this model can use.
campaigns.aria: Attributed revenue per campaign under {{model}}, with the campaigns that cannot carry spend shown in grey.

comparison.title: What the choice of model is worth
comparison.subtitle: The same campaigns under every model that can be computed
comparison.headline: On {{count}} campaigns the choice of model moves the figure by more than a fifth. Neither figure should be quoted as what the campaign earned.
comparison.agree: The models agree closely here, so the choice between them changes little for this period.
comparison.caveat: These are alternative accounts of the same money, so they are shown side by side rather than stacked — adding them would produce a total that exists nowhere. A campaign missing from one model's rows is shown as a gap rather than a zero when that model's breakdown was cut short by the row limit.
comparison.emptyBody: No campaign was credited by any model in this period.
comparison.aria: Attributed revenue per campaign under each available model, grouped so the models can be compared without being added together.

creative.title: Creative Hub
creative.subtitle: Briefs, the versions produced for them, what each file measures against the platform's own requirements, and who signed off on which one.
creative.loadFailed: Could not load the creative board. Try again in a moment.

denied.title: The Creative Hub is not part of your access
denied.body: It carries internal notes and work nobody has approved yet. Ask a workspace owner if you need it.

workload.title: Where the work sits
workload.subtitle: Requests per stage, in the order work moves through them
workload.caveat: Cancelled work is left out: it is not a stage work passes through, and counting it would make an abandoned brief look like a bottleneck at the end.
workload.emptyBody: No creative has been briefed for this scope yet.
workload.aria: How many creative requests sit at each stage, darkening towards the end of the process.

coverage.title: What can be checked
coverage.subtitle: The placements with a recorded specification
coverage.why: The platforms do not publish their creative requirements in a form a program can read, so each of these was read off a platform's own page and recorded with the date. Any placement not listed here reports "no spec recorded" — which means work going out on it is not checked against anything.

spec.noSpec: Nobody has recorded a specification for this placement, so nothing was checked. That is a gap in this product, not a problem with the file.
spec.source: Read from the platform's own page on {{date}}, {{days}} days ago.

detail.pickBody: Its brief, its versions and the decisions made on each appear here.
detail.noVersionsBody: There is nothing to check or approve until a version is added.
detail.staleApproval: This request is marked approved, and its newest version has not been decided on. The approval belongs to the earlier file — do not tell the client the latest cut is signed off.
detail.noPlacement: No placement decided, so nothing can be checked against a specification
detail.audienceHint: Chosen every time, never remembered. An internal note reaching the client is not a mistake worth risking.

operations.title: Operations
operations.subtitle: The work the week is made of: what is open, what is late, what nobody has dated, and who is carrying it.
operations.loadFailed: Could not load the board. Try again in a moment.
operations.truncated: Each column shows the first page of its work. The figures above and the charts below are computed over the whole board.

denied.title: The operations board is not part of your access
denied.body: It carries an agency's own reasons for work being blocked and its own estimates. Ask a workspace owner if you need it.

completion.none: Nothing has been finished or abandoned yet, so there is no completion rate to report.
completion.rate: {{rate}} of the {{settled}} tasks that have settled were completed rather than abandoned.

due.title: When the open work is due
due.subtitle: Open tasks by how soon they are due, soonest first
due.caveatClosed: Finished and cancelled work is left out. Work that was late and is now done is history, and counting it would leave an overdue figure nobody could clear.
due.caveatUndated: Work with no due date is its own bar. It is not "later": it is work that cannot be late, and folding the two together is how a board reports a tidy pipeline it does not have.
due.notReportable: {{overdue}} tasks are overdue, but {{undated}} have no due date at all — only {{share}} of the open board carries one, below the {{floor}} this product treats as reportable. Read the overdue figure as a statement about the dated work, not about all of it.
due.emptyBody: There is no open work on this board, so there is nothing to be due.

load.title: Who is carrying the work
load.subtitle: Open tasks per person, stacked by priority
load.aria: Open tasks per person, by priority
load.caveatOpen: Open work only. Finished and cancelled tasks are not a load anybody is carrying.
load.caveatHidden: {{count}} more people are in the table but not drawn, so the chart stays readable.
load.emptyBody: Nobody is carrying anything on this board at the moment.

detail.pickBody: Choose a card to see where it can go, what it is waiting on, and what it is about.
detail.noMoves: There is nowhere for this task to go from here.
detail.reasonHint: The only record of why the work stopped. Somebody will ask about it.

composer.title: New task
composer.clientHint: Leave this internal for the agency's own work.
composer.dueHint: Optional. Left empty, the task is reported as undated rather than given a deadline nobody agreed to.
